title: Native evidence closed schemas v2 (PROPOSED design reference)
description: Closed Draft 2020-12 records for the native evidence contract. Exact typed admission (foundation/canonical.py) precedes validation: integers are exact JSON integer literals, booleans are not integers, no float/exponent/-0, no duplicate keys, no lone surrogates. The import2 wrapper itself is foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/import; these are its native typed payloads plus native context/coverage/protocol records. Revision after Codex review v2: per-language co-located units (WorkspaceUnitV2/UnitMembershipV1), inert generated-file rows with a read-only virtual OUT_DIR, workflow canonical import payloads with native adapter-input shapes, ImportRegistryRowV1, preparedResolution, principal join, StageAuthorityV1. Blind-consumer corrections: the closed TypeScript native context (TypeScriptNativeContextV2 and family, domain native.context.typescript.v2, carrying typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot) and the subject-scope commitment / coverage-admission records.

WorkspaceUnitV1.description: Superseded by WorkspaceUnitV2 (per-language units may share a rootPath). Retained only so the v1 case fixtures remain readable.

RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.description: executionCapableResolution=true means only that prepared products of some execution were consumed as inert data (preparedResolution != none). It is never a host execution grant; the grant is the operational RepoExecutionGrantV1 reference outside Plan.

InertBlobV1.description: Blob reference. mediaType is a declared label and never a trust proof: admissibility is decided by row kind and consumption channel (PO-0).

authorizationRef.description: Operational H(security.repo-execution-grants.v2,{schemaVersion:2,grantRefs:sorted unique v2 grant references}); one admitted grant per preparation owner. Not a semantic Plan field.

CloneSuppressionV1.description: SUPERSEDED DRAFT transport shape; no product admission path. Workflow ReviewDisposition is the sole current candidate suppression record.

D9MappingRowV1.description: Typed detail beside an EXISTING D9 code: the deficiency and nativeCause live in the coverage2 record named by the termination's coverageId. No successor codes.

outsideBoundaryFiles.description: files at or below an admitted boundary (P3): another project's or uncustodied source, disclosed, never scanned and never erased

RuntimeCoverageAdapterInputV1.description: INPUT ADAPTER SHAPE ONLY (was RuntimeCoveragePayloadV1). Never an admitted import payload: the native adapter normalizes it to the single canonical workflow payload before import2 (contract §7).

TestResultsAdapterInputV1.description: INPUT ADAPTER SHAPE ONLY (was TestResultsPayloadV1). Never an admitted import payload: the native adapter normalizes it to the single canonical workflow payload before import2 (contract §7).

HistoryAdapterInputV1.description: INPUT ADAPTER SHAPE ONLY (was HistoryPayloadV1). Never an admitted import payload: the native adapter normalizes it to the single canonical workflow payload before import2 (contract §7).

CustodyExcludedUnitV1.description: a security excludedUnits row (relative form) whose reason is a custody/depth exclusion; DIRECTORY_CUSTODY/DEPTH exclude the directory and everything below it, MARKER_CUSTODY excludes exactly that marker file

AdmittedBoundaryInventoryV1.description: TRUSTED ADMITTED INPUT (P3): the security discovery instrument's authority boundaries for the selected root, converted once by discovery-defaults.boundary_inventory_from_provenance from the ACCEPTed DiscoveryProvenanceV1 (absolute custody locators -> relative scope paths). Never authored by a caller; an operational host composition passes it to discover_units/assign_membership/unit_scope_descriptor.

UnitBoundariesV1.description: boundary provenance of a unit discovery: source `security.discovery` when the admitted inventory was applied, `none` for the standalone pure instrument (not an operational host composition)

TypeScriptModuleResolutionMode.description: The effective moduleResolution the admitted compiler applies. It changes which specifiers resolve, so it is a native-context field and a universe key.

component.description: declaration file name inside the admitted stdlib closure tree, e.g. lib.es2022.d.ts

compilerVersion.description: the semanticVersion of the ADMITTED signed compiler closure manifest; never the output of an unverified `tsc --version`

typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot.description: identity-and-evidence section 3: the 64-hex SUFFIX of the closure2 identity of the admitted kind=stdlib closure, exactly as ToolchainIdentityV1.rustcDevLlvmDigest is the suffix of the kind=rust-dev-llvm closure. A bare DigestHex, never a Sha256Text: the typed prefix belongs to the foundation closure2 identity it was taken from, and `closure2:` + this value must name a retained closure whose recomputed identity equals it.

standardLibraryComponentDigests.description: The COMPLETE declaration-file inventory of the admitted stdlib closure tree, selected or not: one row per `.d.ts` member, `component` = the member basename, `sha256` = its raw digest, sorted by component UTF-8 bytes. Admission refuses a missing row (two different standard libraries could otherwise mint one context) and refuses a tree in which two paths share a basename, because the join would be ambiguous.

libSelection.description: the effective `lib` names the resolved compilerOptions select (after target defaulting), sorted; each must name a retained component

TypeScriptToolClosureV1.description: Every executable the TypeScript adapter may select: the bundled compiler and the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure2 named by closureId. No PATH lookup, no system `node`, no NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH/TS_NODE_* from the environment.

TypeScriptHonoredOptionsV1.description: The closed subset of the resolved compilerOptions that changes program membership, module resolution or checking. Every value is the EFFECTIVE post-resolution value of the admitted tsconfig graph (or of SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1 under js-synthesized), never a raw file field.

configGraphPaths.description: every tsconfig/jsconfig file in the resolved extends graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under configOrigin=synthesized

TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2.description: The TypeScript counterpart of CargoConfigProjectionV2. Stripping an option is disclosed here; it is never a reason to read the option from anywhere else.

TypeScriptNativeContextV2.description: Closed native context for the typescript-v2 universe; H domain `native.context.typescript.v2`. It carries no platform FIELD because TypeScript resolution semantics are platform-invariant by design (section 1.1); the identity is NOT platform-invariant, because toolClosure.closureId names a signed closure whose foundation descriptor includes `platform`, so two platform families running different executables mint two nativeContextIds. It is NOT NativeContextV2, which is the Rust context (targetTriple/hostTriple/cargo resolver); a typescript-v2 universe whose nativeContextId was minted from a Rust descriptor is refused.

NativeContextLanguageV1.description: which closed native-context record and H domain a universe binds

NativeContextAdmissionV1.description: Host result of admitting one native context. nativeContextId is the Sha256Text the universe carries; planNativeContextDigest is the same 64 hex without the prefix, the spelling foundation plan.nativeContextDigests requires.

SubjectScopeCommitmentV1.description: The producing result for the retained c2-plan-stage-schema.v4 coverage key field. subjectScopeCommitment is the SAME 64 hex as the foundation subject-scope identity scopeId, re-spelled in the native Sha256Text text form; it introduces no second preimage and no native H domain.

CoverageAdmissionV1.description: Result of the admitted native producer boundary for one CoverageResultV3 payload: the host mints scope2 from its own subject enumeration and refuses a payload whose committed key disagrees. A provider-supplied commitment is never authority.
